title: The Late Summer Again
premise: Petra Coldharbour, once the most sought-after wedding planner on the coast, now runs a small events business in the quiet town of Late Summer Bay, hiding from the scandal that ended her engagement seven years ago. When a snowstorm traps her at a mountain inn with Julian Voss—her former business partner, rival, and the man she betrayed to save her own reputation—the carefully sealed past begins thawing. Forced to co-plan one last impossible wedding for a couple who remind them of who they used to be, Petra and Julian must untangle old lies, including the truth that Julian took the blame for her mistake all those years ago. In the end, Petra publicly confesses, loses the contract she fought to keep, and gains something larger: forgiveness from Julian, reconciliation with her estranged sister, and a second chance at love measured not in safe steps but in honest ones.
about_author: W. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former hospitality professional who spent a decade coordinating weddings before turning to fiction. Hartwell writes romance set in coastal towns, drawn to stories about people who rebuild their lives quietly and then must decide whether to let someone in.

chapters.title: The Weather in Her Hands
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Seven years after fleeing the industry, Petra plans a modest anniversary party in Late Summer Bay, controlling every detail because control is all she trusts. A call comes: an old client wants her for a destination wedding—but so does her rival. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of a life built on small safe steps.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept the Ledger
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian Voss arrives in town to scout venues, carrying a worn notebook of every debt he believes he's owed—including one from Petra. He tells himself this bid is business, nothing more. Emotional beat: resentment disguised as professionalism, and the ache of unfinished history.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Contract
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The client, Delia Marsh, announces she's hired both planners jointly or neither. Petra and Julian sign under protest, trading barbed courtesies across a conference table. Emotional beat: forced proximity as a slow-burning fuse; neither will be first to walk away.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Venue scouting along the coast; Julian watches Petra work and remembers why he loved her at twenty-five. A near-honest conversation dies when she deflects with logistics. Emotional beat: nostalgia weaponized against itself—he can't tell if he wants closure or her.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Stopped Calling
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra's sister Rowan visits unannounced, pressing her to attend their mother's sixtieth birthday—a family Petra abandoned after the scandal. Rowan drops a detail about Julian that doesn't fit Petra's memory of him. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like driftwood after a storm.

chapters.title: Snowfall at Hollow Pine
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The wedding party travels to a mountain lodge for the rehearsal weekend; a sudden blizzard closes the pass, stranding Petra, Julian, Delia, and guests with no cell service. Emotional beat: the outside world cut off, leaving only the two of them and everything unsaid.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Rooms
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Trapped indoors, Petra and Julian are assigned adjoining rooms and end up sharing a fire when the power flickers. Old jokes return unbidden. She catches herself laughing and hates how easy it feels. Emotional beat: warmth as threat—the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Wine, storm-dark windows, and one reckless kiss that both of them initiate and neither stops. Morning brings silence and separate breakfasts. Emotional beat: desire outrunning duty, followed immediately by the cost of it.

chapters.title: Delia Knows
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Sharp-eyed bride Delia confronts Petra privately: she chose them both deliberately, having heard rumors of what happened between them years ago. She gives Petra three days to fix whatever it is, or she pulls the wedding. Emotional beat: deadline pressure; secrets have witnesses.

chapters.title: The Version He Told Himself
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian finally voices his grievance: Petra sold out their company, took the client list, and vanished while he absorbed the fallout. Petra goes white—because that isn't what happened. But she says nothing. Emotional beat: the lie of omission hardening into a wall.

chapters.title: Rowan's Letter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A letter forwarded from Rowan reveals the truth Petra buried: it was Petra's fiancé who forged the contracts, and Julian covered for her at the hearing without her knowledge. She realizes he sacrificed his career believing she'd abandoned him knowingly. Emotional beat: vertigo—her whole narrative collapses.

chapters.title: Confession in a Frozen Garden
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Petra finds Julian alone and tells him everything: the forgery, her shame, the years of invisibility. His fury is quiet and worse than shouting—you knew, and you let me hate you. Emotional beat: truth offered too late; trust broken in a new place.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Without a Bride
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Delia's three days expire; she cancels the wedding, citing 'unresolved conflicts.' Julian, professionally ruined again by association, packs to leave. Petra begs him to stay; he refuses. Emotional beat: rock bottom—the mistake repeated in a new key.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Alone, Petra faces the pattern: she has always chosen disappearance over repair—with Julian, with Rowan, with herself. She writes the confession she should have given seven years ago and sends copies to everyone she wronged. Emotional beat: forgiveness of self begins where excuses end.

chapters.title: What Julian Carried
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. On the road home, Julian reads his old ledger and realizes every entry was a way of avoiding his own failure—that he never asked Petra the real questions because he preferred being wronged to being unsure. Emotional beat: the rival discovers his own half of the debt.

chapters.title: Delia's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Delia calls: the wedding is back on—if Petra plans it solo and tells the assembled guests the truth about why it nearly collapsed. Public confession as price of redemption. Petra accepts. Emotional beat: courage with a countdown clock attached.

chapters.title: Late Summer, Out of Season
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian returns to town intending only to collect his things, but finds the bay preparing for the wedding—and hears from Rowan what Petra gave up to make her confession. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions until they point the same way.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the reception, Petra stands before two hundred guests and tells the whole story—the forgery, the flight, the man who paid for her silence with his career. Julian listens from the back. Emotional beat: climax; vulnerability as the bravest act left.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian crosses out the final entry in his notebook and tears the page out. He finds Petra on the terrace afterward; there is no grand speech, only the question he should have asked seven years ago: what do you want now? Emotional beat: release; the war ends by surrender on both sides.

chapters.title: Rowan at the Door
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Reconciliation with Rowan and, by phone, a cautious first step toward her mother. Petra declines a lucrative offer to return to the big-city industry, choosing instead to build something small and true in the bay. Emotional beat: found family restored; ambition redefined.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Believing In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later, Petra and Julian co-plan one final event—not a client's wedding but a tiny ceremony of their own on the beach at late summer, with Rowan as witness and Delia gleefully meddling. Emotional beat: joy earned rather than escaped into.

chapters.title: Again, From the Beginning
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, closing. On their first anniversary, Petra finds Julian's old notebook framed above their desk, last page torn out, replaced with a new blank ledger titled 'Us.' She adds the first entry: a date, a tide chart, no conditions. Emotional beat: resolution—love as a practice, begun again daily.
